draft.title: Electric shock
card: An electric shock happens when current passes through the body. Current, not voltage alone, causes the harm.

The harm grows with the size of the current and with how long it flows. Current is roughly V ÷ R, so lower body resistance lets more current flow at the same voltage. Wet skin has a lower resistance than dry skin.
Effects range from a tingle and muscle spasms to burns and the heart beating abnormally. A current of around 0.1 A or more through the chest can be fatal.
First aid: switch off the power, or free the person using a non-conductor such as dry wood. Do not touch them while they are still in contact. Then call 000, and start CPR if they are not breathing.
draft.remember: Harm depends on current and time, so cut the power first and then get help.

a.q: Two people touch the same faulty wiring at the same voltage. Why might one receive a larger current than the other?
opts: Their body resistances differ, such as wet and dry skin
Only the person with dry skin has current pass through
Current depends only on the voltage, so it must be equal
Wet skin has a higher resistance, so it carries more current
a.why: At the same voltage, current is roughly V ÷ R, so lower resistance gives more current. Wet skin has a lower resistance than dry skin. The option saying current depends only on voltage ignores resistance.
a.clue: Think of I = V ÷ R with a different R.

b.q: Jai finds his friend gripping a damaged power cord and unable to let go. The power point is nearby. What should Jai do first?
opts: Switch off the power at the power point
Pull his friend away from the cord by the arm
Call 000 and wait beside his friend for help
Start CPR while his friend still holds the cord
b.why: Cutting the power stops the current and keeps Jai safe. Pulling his friend by the arm is tempting, but Jai could become part of the circuit and be shocked too. Calling 000 and CPR come after the danger is removed.
b.clue: Remove the danger before helping, so you are not shocked too.

a.best: Their body resistances differ, such as wet and dry skin

b.best: Switch off the power at the power point

problems.detail: Two of the wrong options carry absolute words ('Only', 'only... must'), so a student can rule them out without knowing the idea. The right option is also the only one with a worked example ('such as wet and dry skin').
The clue 'Think of I = V ÷ R with a different R' all but states the answer, that resistance differs.
